rulings.challenge_claim: This unit's content sits inside the same flagged narrative-overlap block as the immediately preceding unit but, unlike that unit, discloses no relationship to the closing appendix's parallel account of the same events; no apparatus mark inside the span compensates for the gap.
rulings.grounds: The factual premise holds and the apparatus premise holds; the disclosure duty does not. The burning of the city, the deportation and the provision for the poor are reported a second time at the corresponding point of the closing appendix (web:Jer.52.13, web:Jer.52.14, web:Jer.52.15, web:Jer.52.16), and across MT 39:8-39:10 the parashah, paseq, ketiv/qere and special-letter inventories are all empty, so nothing enumerated is owed inside the span and nothing is over-claimed. But the appendix relation is typed-relation metadata whose ruled standing is never boundary evidence and never counterevidence; the neighbouring unit's note is worded precisely to withhold evidentiary weight, so it creates no disclosure object whose symmetry can be swept the way the mark, ketiv/qere and island layers are swept. A note that carries no evidentiary force cannot generate an omission defect elsewhere, and the item cites no bytes and no ref for the duty it asserts. What is defective in the very field the item points at is adjacent and checkable: device_notes argues that the guard-captain's title is carried forward by 'the following span', a positional cross-reference, where the title in fact stands as רַב טַבָּחִ֖ים (oshb:Jer.39.11, byte) and again at oshb:Jer.39.13, neither of which appears in boundary_evidence_refs, though that field does carry oshb:Jer.39.7 for the front seam. A verse argued in prose outside the row's own span belongs in the refs, and a cross-row reference is verse-anchored, not positional. Second, undetected by either item: the quotation of web:Jer.39.8 in boundary_rationale renders the staged text's two right single quotation marks as straight typewriter apostrophes, in 'king's' and in 'people's' - the straight-for-curly class; the unit's other two renderings, of web:Jer.39.9 and web:Jer.39.10, are character-exact against the staged text. The challenge as framed drops to low; the row's final weight is set by that quote-fidelity defect, which is the same class this material carries at medium elsewhere.
rulings.remedy: Three orders. (1) In device_notes, replace the positional forward reference with a verse-anchored one naming oshb:Jer.39.11 and oshb:Jer.39.13, and add both refs to boundary_evidence_refs; test: no positional or relative cross-row wording survives in any field, and every verse argued outside Jer.39.8-Jer.39.10 resolves inside boundary_evidence_refs. (2) In boundary_rationale, restore the two right single quotation marks inside the web:Jer.39.8 rendering; test: the quoted run matches the staged verse text character-for-character with no straightening applied - the test the original fails. (3) No appendix-relationship note is owed; if one is added anyway it stays prose-only, with no structured ref, no entry in boundary_evidence_refs and no boundary role.

rulings.challenge_claim: A ketiv/qere note at MT 39:12, inside this unit's own span, goes wholly undisclosed while the special letter at 39:13 and the setumah at 39:14 are disclosed correctly; and the roster is said to name four officers, a digit the bytes it cites contradict.
rulings.grounds: Both items stand, and they are distinct defects rather than one. The ketiv/qere inventory records a note at MT 39:12, inside Jer.39.11-Jer.39.14. The unit engages two other apparatus classes in the same short span - the book's one special-letter seg at MT 39:13 (inventory: 1 site book-wide) and the setumah at MT 39:14 - so the layer is live here and symmetry is completed by sweeping the span, not by spot-citing the verses the prose happens to reach; MT 39:12 is reached by no sentence and by no individual ref, appearing only inside the outer range citation, while boundary_evidence_refs itemises oshb:Jer.39.10, oshb:Jer.39.11, oshb:Jer.39.13 and oshb:Jer.39.14 around it. The officer digit is independently defective. MT 39:13 names three officers, each carrying his own title - נְבֽוּזַרְאֲדָ֣ן רַב טַבָּחִ֗ים וּנְבֽוּשַׁזְבָּן֙ רַב סָרִ֔יס וְנֵרְגַ֥ל שַׂר אֶ֖צֶר רַב מָ֑ג (oshb:Jer.39.13, byte) - and then a collective body, וְכֹ֖ל רַבֵּ֥י מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶֽל (oshb:Jer.39.13, byte). The staged rendering quoted beside the digit yields no four-member list either, and the digit names no count object before counting, so it fails the bytes in both witnesses and the name-the-object-first rule at once. Sound and to be preserved: the special-letter handling is exact - the seg is x-small, disclosed single-witness, and the verse carries exactly one word ending in a final nun bearing the seg's accent (count: 1 in-verse), the second officer's name, so the attribution is byte-determinable rather than assumed; the resh-family royal spelling and the guard-captain title are right per site. Lesser finding neither item raises: device_notes claims a fuller patronymic than any other figure sharing the name and points to that other bearer as 'named earlier', with no verse anchor and no sweep digit; the comparandum stands at oshb:Jer.38.1, which is argued in prose but absent from boundary_evidence_refs.
rulings.remedy: Three orders. (1) In boundary_rationale, disclose the ketiv/qere note at MT 39:12, single-witness, marked present-but-not-engaged if no splice reaches it, and add oshb:Jer.39.12 to boundary_evidence_refs; test: every ketiv/qere verse inside Jer.39.11-Jer.39.14 is disclosed, checked by sweeping the span's inventory rather than by spot cite. (2) In boundary_rationale, replace 'names four officers' with the named count object and its byte-supported digit - three officers each carrying his own title, followed by the collective body of the king of Babylon's chief officers; test: the digit is reproducible from oshb:Jer.39.13's own bytes and from the staged rendering quoted beside it. (3) In device_notes, verse-anchor the comparandum at oshb:Jer.38.1, add that ref to boundary_evidence_refs, and either carry a digit-bearing sweep for the 'any other' comparison or drop the exclusivity wording; test: no exclusivity claim stands without an adjacent digit, and no unanchored positional cross-reference remains in any field.

rulings.challenge_claim: One item: the unit's own rendering of verse 18 carries straight typewriter marks where the staged text carries curly ones, and the resumptive, pre-fall timing of verse 15 goes undrawn. The other: the opening-seam warrant misdescribes the word-event system - the shape it contrasts 39:15 against is not verb-initial and the system counts three shapes, not two - while the declared title stack is never quoted and the closure token at 39:17 and 39:18 is never named.
rulings.grounds: The word-event item is upheld and can be put more sharply. Of the three counted shapes (21, 11 and 4 verses) exactly one, the narrative-onset shape, is verb-initial (1 of 3). The superscription shape opens with the article-noun and stands its verb third - הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה (oshb:Jer.40.1, byte) - and the topical-header shape opens with the relative particle; the counted inventory further separates the three as different unit classes, narrative onset against prose-sermon superscription against topical header, so calling them 'the book's two counted narrative shapes' both undercounts the system and mis-classes the shape it names. The non-membership finding survives intact: 39:15 fronts a prepositional addressee phrase ahead of the verb - וְאֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הָיָ֣ה דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.39.15, byte) - and belongs to none of the three. The form-label is also wrong: that fronted element is not the object, and the clause subject is the word-of-YHWH phrase itself. The declared-signal item is upheld and extends further than stated: the full signature title stack stands at כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.39.16, byte) and is never quoted, tier-labelled or mouth-named, and the unit's rendering of that verse is cut with an inserted ellipsis - a character the staged text does not carry - at exactly the point where the staged rendering goes on to render that stack, so the sole speech-formula entry among this unit's 2 declared signals loses its evidence in both languages at once. The closure token does stand at MT 39:17 and MT 39:18 (2 verses in span), unnamed; at 162 verses book-wide it is closure corroboration only, so that is under-engagement, not a missing driver. The quote-fidelity item is upheld and under-counted: the rendering of web:Jer.39.18 degrades four marks, not two - the contraction in 'won't', the mark closing the embedded clause after 'trust in me,', and both marks in the trailing pair after 'says Yahweh' - and a fifth degraded mark stands in the rendering of web:Jer.39.15, in 'Yahweh's', which no item names. The resumption point is refuted as a defect: the pre-fall setting argues for this cut rather than against it, and the disclosed cohesion duty runs to byte-true devices straddling the seam that argue continuity against the row, so its absence is an unused corroboration, not an omission. Confirmed sound: the ketiv/qere note at MT 39:16 is disclosed present-but-not-engaged and correctly scoped, since the rendering stops before it, and the setumah marks at MT 39:14 and MT 39:18 verify under their own type.
rulings.remedy: Four orders. (1) In boundary_rationale, correct the contrast: name the three counted shapes and state that exactly one of them is verb-initial, or drop the verb-initial comparison and keep only the byte-true non-membership finding; test: every shape-class statement is reproducible from the counted inventory's own verse sets and from the opening word of each shape's bytes. (2) In boundary_rationale, re-label the fronted element as a prepositional addressee phrase, not the object, and name the word-of-YHWH phrase as the clause subject; test: the form-label is checkable against oshb:Jer.39.15's pointed bytes. (3) In boundary_rationale, quote the 39:16 formula in pointed Hebrew with its tier and its mouth named and re-cut the English rendering so the declared signal's own words are not what the ellipsis removes, or else drop speech_formula.koh_amar_yhwh_tsevaot_elohei_yisrael from observed_substrate_signals; test: every declared substrate signal has a quoted, tier-labelled form in the prose, and no quoted run carries a character the staged text lacks. (4) In boundary_rationale, restore all five staged marks in the web:Jer.39.15 and web:Jer.39.18 renderings; test: each quoted run matches the staged verse text character-for-character with no straightening applied. No change is owed for the pre-fall timing observation.

rulings.challenge_claim: One item: the device note asserts that Gedaliah is not named in this stretch, though the name stands inside the unit's own byte-tier splice of 40:5, and the paseq inside the span is undisclosed while the ketiv/qere in the same span is disclosed. The other: the header-shape argument is well grounded, but two renderings carry straight marks where the source carries curly ones, and the paseq at 40:1 goes unmentioned.
rulings.grounds: The naming defect is real, is the heaviest in this material, and is self-refuting in-row. MT 40:5 reads אֶל גְּדַלְיָ֣ה בֶן אֲחִיקָ֣ם בֶּן שָׁפָ֡ן (oshb:Jer.40.5, byte): the personal name stands immediately before the patronymic that device_notes offers as kinship-only pointing, and it stands inside the full-verse splice the unit itself carries at byte tier in boundary_rationale. The staged rendering of the same verse names him as well, and the unit's English quotation of 40:5 is cut back to its closing sentence, so the rendering that would have exposed the error is the part not shown. The claim is therefore false in both witnesses and contradicted by the unit's own quoted evidence, and it carries an unanchored positional forward reference to the unit that follows on top of that. High severity is right. The apparatus item is also upheld: the paseq inventory records a seg at MT 40:1, inside Jer.40.1-Jer.40.5, and the unit discloses the ketiv/qere at MT 40:3 and the preceding setumah at MT 39:18, so the layer is engaged and the sweep is owed across the span. The quote-fidelity item is upheld and under-counted: three marks are degraded, not two - the opening mark of the embedded speech in the web:Jer.40.2 rendering, and in the web:Jer.40.4 rendering both the contraction in 'don't' and the closing mark after 'go there'. Sound and to be preserved: the header's membership in the eleven-verse superscription shape is byte-correct at oshb:Jer.40.1, carrying the aleph-lamed form rather than the one-site variant; disclosing that the shape frames a release narrative rather than sermon content, instead of letting the formula name the unit, is the right handling and should survive the repair; and the renderings of web:Jer.40.1, web:Jer.40.5 and web:Jer.40.6 are character-exact, the 40:5 one at a live continuation-fold verse.
rulings.remedy: Three orders. (1) In device_notes, strike the claim that Gedaliah is not yet named in this stretch; if the kinship observation is kept at all, re-cut it to the bytes - both the personal name and the two-generation patronymic stand at oshb:Jer.40.5 - and verse-anchor any forward reference instead of naming the unit that follows; test: every name-presence claim is checkable against the unit's own splice and against the staged rendering of the cited verse, which is the check the original fails. (2) In boundary_rationale, disclose the paseq at MT 40:1, single-witness, seg-layer, count-only, with no intra-verse position asserted; test: the span's paseq inventory is swept, not spot-cited. (3) In boundary_rationale, restore the three staged marks in the web:Jer.40.2 and web:Jer.40.4 renderings; test: each quoted run matches the staged verse text character-for-character with no straightening applied.

rulings.challenge_claim: One item: a paseq at MT 40:7 inside the span is not mentioned while the ketiv/qere and paseq at MT 40:8 are disclosed together, and the rendering of verse 9 opens the embedded speech with a straight mark. The other: the same 40:7 omission, with the device note's wording that apparatus converges at 40:8 read as a uniqueness claim the inventory does not support.
rulings.grounds: The omission is upheld; the uniqueness reading is not. The paseq inventory records a seg at MT 40:7 and another at MT 40:8, both inside Jer.40.7-Jer.40.10; the unit discloses only the second, and it quotes MT 40:7 in full in the same field, so the verse is squarely inside its attention and the layer is explicitly engaged - symmetry here is completed by sweeping the span. But the device note's sentence, that two apparatus classes converge at 40:8, is byte-true as written: MT 40:8 alone in this span carries both a ketiv/qere pair and a paseq (inventory across Jer.40.7-Jer.40.10: 2 paseq segs, 1 ketiv/qere note), and the sentence asserts a co-occurrence, not the exclusive presence of the paseq layer. The defect is the missing 40:7 disclosure, not the convergence wording, and the sentence should be preserved rather than rewritten once the omission is cured. Severity is medium rather than low: this layer's disclosure symmetry is unconditional and the omitted verse is quoted in full in the field that engages the layer. The quote-fidelity item is upheld and under-counted: three marks are degraded, not one - in the web:Jer.40.9 rendering both the opening mark of the sworn assurance and the contraction in 'Don't', and in the web:Jer.40.10 rendering the closing mark after 'you have taken', which no item names. Sound and to be preserved: the ketiv/qere at MT 40:8 is stated in the right direction, written form before read form, both standing in the verse's own bytes, and labelled single-witness; the setumah at MT 40:6 verifies under its own type with no petuchah conflated into it; and the referent split between the Chaldeans and the king of Babylon in adjacent clauses of oshb:Jer.40.9 is byte-true. Lesser finding neither item raises: the ketiv/qere disclosure is spliced into the middle of the sentence that introduces the named arrivals, leaving that sentence ungrammatical in the stored prose.
rulings.remedy: Three orders. (1) In boundary_rationale, disclose the paseq at MT 40:7 beside the one at MT 40:8, single-witness, seg-layer, count-only, no intra-verse position; keep the existing convergence sentence, which is byte-true, and let it claim the two-class co-occurrence at 40:8 only; test: the paseq inventory for Jer.40.7-Jer.40.10 is swept and every disclosed seg is count-only. (2) In boundary_rationale, restore the three staged marks in the web:Jer.40.9 and web:Jer.40.10 renderings; test: each quoted run matches the staged verse text character-for-character with no straightening applied. (3) In boundary_rationale, repair the sentence carrying the ketiv/qere disclosure so the disclosure stands as its own clause rather than interrupting the naming sentence; test: the sentence parses on its own and the disclosure keeps its single-witness label.
